# ServisFirst Bancshares, Inc. Announces Results for Third Quarter of 2026


October 19, 2026 4:04pm EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_9a317fb1c185dbb9924ecf79f158b94e/servisfirstbank/news/2026-10-19_ServisFirst_Bancshares_Inc_Announces_Results_for_269.pdf)

[Earnings Webcast](https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=aooOfwiw)


[Audio](https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=aooOfwiw)


BIRMINGHAM, Ala., Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ServisFirst Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: SFBS) today announced earnings and operating results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights and Financial Summary:**


- **Diluted earnings per share of $0.80 for the quarter, up 33% from the third quarter of 2025, and up 23% from adjusted diluted earnings per share in the third quarter of 2025*.**
- **Loans grew by $1.43 billion, or 11%, year-over-year** .
- **Net interest margin of 3.63%, unchanged from the second quarter of 2026; excluding a loan recovery in the previous quarter, NIM was 5 basis points higher, and up 54 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025.**
- **Noninterest-bearing deposits increased 12% year-over-year.**
- **Completed our two-for-one stock split during the quarter**.**
- **Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company announced its inaugural stock repurchase program, authorizing the repurchase of up to two million shares of common stock through December 31, 2027.**
- **Book value per share of $18.63, up 14% year-over-year.**
- **Efficiency ratio of 30.20%, improved from 35.22% in the third quarter of 2025.**
- **Year-to-date return on average common stockholders’ equity increased from 15.01% in 2025 to 17.62% in 2026, and year-to-date adjusted return on average common stockholders’ equity* increased from 15.85% to 17.61%.**
- **Consolidated common equity tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets increased from 11.49% in the third quarter of 2025 to 11.98% in the third quarter of 2026.**


Tom Broughton, Chairman, President, and CEO, said, “We see solid economic trends, and loan activity is improving with continued growth in our loan pipeline.”


David Sparacio, CFO, said, “We continue to grow our top line revenue through asset and margin growth, while maintaining a best-in-class efficiency ratio, resulting in top quartile returns.”

**DETAILED FINANCIALS**


ServisFirst Bancshares, Inc. reported net income and net income available to common stockholders of $87.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $65.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Basic and diluted earnings per common share were both $0.80 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.78 in the second quarter of 2026 and $0.60 in the third quarter of 2025. The prior-year quarter adjusted diluted earnings per share were $0.65.


Annualized return on average assets was1.89% and annualized return on average common stockholders’ equity was 17.26% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.47% and 14.88%, respectively, for the third quarter of 2025.


Net interest income was $159.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $155.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $133.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The net interest margin in the third quarter of 2026 was 3.63% compared to 3.63% in the second quarter of 2026 and 3.09% in the third quarter of 2025. Loan yields were 6.24% during the third quarter of 2026 compared to 6.23% during the second quarter of 2026 and 6.34% during the third quarter of 2025. During the second quarter of 2026, we recovered $1.9 million in interest income from a large credit relationship that was previously on nonaccrual status. This recovery accounted for five basis points of the increase in loan yields from the first quarter of 2026. Investment yields were 3.85% during the third quarter of 2026 compared to 3.82% during the second quarter of 2026 and 3.60% during the third quarter of 2025. Average interest-bearing deposit rates were 2.80% during the third quarter of 2026, compared to 2.80% during the second quarter of 2026 and 3.41% during the third quarter of 2025. Average federal funds purchased rates were 3.78% during the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.74% during the second quarter of 2026 and 4.46% during the third quarter of 2025.


Average loans for the third quarter of 2026 were $14.54 billion, an increase of $320.5 million, or 8.9% annualized, from average loans of $14.22 billion for the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of $1.34 billion, or 10.1%, from average loans of $13.21 billion for the third quarter of 2025. Ending total loans for the third quarter of 2026 were $14.74 billion, an increase of $258.8 million, or 7.1% annualized, from $14.48 billion for the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of $1.43 billion, or 10.7%, from $13.31 billion for the third quarter of 2025.


Average total deposits for the third quarter of 2026 were $14.33 billion, an increase of $10.6 million, or 0.3% annualized, from average total deposits of $14.32 billion for the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of $195.2 million, or 1.4%, from average total deposits of $14.13 billion for the third quarter of 2025. Ending total deposits for the third quarter of 2026 were $14.09 billion, a decrease of $461.4 million, or 12.6% annualized, from $14.55 billion for the second quarter of 2026, and a decrease of $19.5 million, or 0.1%, from $14.11 billion for the third quarter of 2025.


Nonperforming assets to total assets were 0.96% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 0.96% for the second quarter of 2026 and 0.96% for the third quarter of 2025. Annualized net charge-offs to average loans were 0.21% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 0.11% for the second quarter of 2026 and 0.27% for the third quarter of 2025. The allowance for credit losses to total loans at September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, was 1.28%, 1.26%, and 1.28%, respectively. We recorded a $14.9 million provision for loan losses in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $11.7 million in the second quarter of 2026, and $9.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.


Noninterest income was $13.1 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $2.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of $10.3 million. Adjusted for $148,000 of securities gains in the third of 2026 and $7.8 million of securities losses in the third quarter of 2025, this represented a $2.3 million, or 21.8% increase. Service charges on deposit accounts increased $132,000, or 4.0%, to $3.4 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $3.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $110,000, or 3.3% on a linked quarter basis. Mortgage banking revenue remained relatively flat at $1.9 million, on a year-over-year basis. Credit card income remained relatively flat at $2.4 million, on a year-over-year basis. Bank-owned life insurance (“BOLI”) income increased $1.9 million, or 80.6%, to $4.3 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $2.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $210,000, or 5.1%, on a linked quarter basis. Other operating income increased $174,000, or 26.6%, to $829,000 for the third quarter of 2026 from $655,000 in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $121,000, or 17.1%, on a linked quarter basis.


Noninterest expense increased $4.2 million, or 8.8%, to $52.2 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $48.0 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $2.3 million, or 4.5%, on a linked quarter basis. Salary and benefit expense increased $1.4 million, or 5.5%, to $26.9 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $25.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $653,000, or 2.5%, on a linked quarter basis. The year-over-year increase was primarily due to the full impact of our Houston market expansion. The number of full-time equivalent employees (excluding temporary employees) increased by 25, or 3.8%, to 675 at September 30, 2026 compared to 650 at September 30, 2025, and increased by twelve from the end of the second quarter of 2026. Equipment and occupancy expense decreased $234,000, or 6.5%, to $3.4 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $3.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and decreased $582,000, or 14.7%, on a linked quarter basis. Third party processing and other services expense decreased $14,000, or 0.2%, to $8.1 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $8.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $119,000, or 1.5%, on a linked quarter basis. Professional services expense increased $94,000, or 5.1%, to $2.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, and decreased $276,000, or 12.4%, on a linked quarter basis. Other operating expenses increased $2.9 million, or 46.9%, to $8.9 million for the third quarter of 2026 from $6.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and increased $2.2 million, or 33.2%, on a linked quarter basis. The efficiency ratio was 30.20% during the third quarter of 2026 compared to 35.22% during the third quarter of 2025 and 29.65% during the second quarter of 2026.


Our effective tax rate was 17.21% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 16.81% for the third quarter of 2025, and 19.94% on a linked quarter basis. During the third quarter of 2026, we purchased Investment Tax Credits, which reduced our tax expense. We recognized a reduction in provision for income taxes resulting from excess tax benefits from the exercise and vesting of stock options and restricted stock during the third quarters of 2026 and 2025 of $37,000 and $81,000, respectively.


**About ServisFirst Bancshares, Inc.**


ServisFirst Bancshares, Inc. (the “Company”) is a bank holding company based in Birmingham, Alabama. Through its subsidiary ServisFirst Bank (the “Bank”), the Company provides business and personal financial services from locations in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, North and South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Virginia. Through the Bank, we originate commercial, consumer and other loans and accept deposits, provide electronic banking services, such as online and mobile banking, including remote deposit capture, deliver treasury and cash management services and provide correspondent banking services to other financial institutions.

**GAAP Reconciliation and Management Explanation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


This press release contains the non-GAAP financial measures of tangible common stockholders’ equity, total tangible assets, tangible book value per share and tangible common equity to total tangible assets, each of which excludes goodwill associated with our acquisition of Metro Bancshares, Inc. in January 2015. We recognized an $8.6 million loss on sale of available-for-sale debt securities in noninterest income during the second quarter of 2025 due to restructuring the portfolio. We reversed a $2.3 million legal reserve from interest expense during the second quarter of 2025. We recognized a $7.8 million loss on sale of available-for-sale debt securities in non-interest income during the third quarter of 2025 due to continued restructuring of the portfolio. These adjustments to our results are to reflect items unusual, or infrequent, in nature and are not considered to be part of our non-interest expense, run rate. Each of adjusted net income, adjusted net income available to common stockholders, adjusted diluted earnings per share, adjusted net interest income, adjusted return on average assets, adjusted return on average common stockholders’ equity, and adjusted efficiency ratio excludes the impact of this, net of tax, and are all considered non-GAAP financial measures. This press release also contains the non-GAAP financial measures of adjusted net income, adjusted net income available to common stockholders, adjusted diluted earnings per share, adjusted return on average assets, adjusted return on average common stockholders’ equity, adjusted efficiency ratio, adjusted net interest income, adjusted noninterest income, and adjusted noninterest expense.


We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to management and investors that is supplementary to our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows computed in accordance with GAAP; however, we acknowledge that these non-GAAP financial measures have limitations.
